item.title: Vance appears to soften U.S. demands on Iranian nuclear enrichment
item.description: Vance says Iran must do "something meaningful on enrichment capacity" to end the war, as Rubio claims Tehran has "lost complete control" of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Stock markets hit record high despite inflation, high fuel prices
item.description: U.S. stock markets hit a record high Tuesday amid major inflation and skyrocketing fuel prices. CBS News business analyst Jill Schlesinger breaks down how you can respond.

item.title: Israelis, Palestinians reflect on 3 years since Oct. 7 attacks
item.description: Wednesday marks three years since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attacks. Holly Williams has more.

item.title: Tropical Storm Isaias forms in Gulf, could reach U.S. as hurricane this weekend
item.description: Tropical Storm Isaias has formed in the Gulf and is expected to become a hurricane by Thursday before approaching the U.S. northern Gulf Coast on Friday, according to forecasters.

item.title: Trump temporarily expands use of red-dyed diesel. Will it lower costs?
item.description: Experts say the new executive order will have a limited impact on farmers and truckers who rely on diesel.

item.title: Congress tried to fix issues with surprise medical costs. It created another problem.
item.description: The No Surprises Act, which was passed by Congress in 2020, was meant to help protect patients from surprise bills. Years later, it's caused unintended consequences that directly impact patients. Anna Schecter reports.

item.title: Former Israeli hostage says Netanyahu is "unworthy" of his position
item.description: Liat Atzili and her husband were taken hostage by Hamas militants on Oct. 7, 2023. Atzili returned home; her husband was killed. Three years later, Atzili and her cousin, filmmaker Brandon Kramer, reflect on her experience, which is the subject of a documentary Kramer directed.

item.title: Couple caught in California surrogacy scandal arrested
item.description: A California couple at the center of a surrogacy scandal was arrested Tuesday on charges related to the case. Jonathan Vigliotti has more.

item.title: Flu season got an early start. Here's what to know.
item.description: Flu season got off to an early start this year, with the CDC noticing a jump in emergency room visits from the virus. Dr. Céline Gounder joins the show with what to know about this year's strain.

item.title: Wars and grief in the Middle East in the aftermath of Oct. 7 attacks
item.description: The Oct. 7, 2023, attacks in Israel helped fuel a series of conflicts in the Middle East, from Israel's wars in Gaza and Lebanon to the collapse of the Syrian regime and the U.S. war in Iran. CBS News' Holly Williams reports.

item.title: Surrogate urges "laws, regulations" after couple arrested on child abuse charges
item.description: A California couple at the center of a surrogacy scandal has been arrested on child abuse charges. CBS News legal reporter Katrina Kaufman reports.

item.title: Father of IDF soldier killed in Oct. 7 attacks marks 3 years: "We live it each day"
item.description: Ruby Chen, the father of IDF soldier Itay Chen, who was taken hostage by Hamas on Oct. 7, 2023, and later died, marks three years since the attacks and the first year since all the hostages, living and dead, were returned to Israel.

item.title: Christa Pike awake and talking after botched execution, lawyers say
item.description: Death row inmate Christa Pike survived two doses of a lethal injection drug and is awake and talking, her lawyers say. CBS News' Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: Space station crew returns home after eight-month mission
item.description: Two NASA astronauts, a European flier and a Russian cosmonaut will close out an eight-month mission with splashdown Thursday.

item.title: Cornell professor alleges efforts to keep rape allegations "as quiet as possible"
item.description: The Cornell University community was rocked after an anonymous student known as Jane Doe alleges she was raped by members of a fraternity at the school and claims the university and others failed to protect her. CBS News' Lilia Luciano reports.

item.title: "The Perfect Line" host Deborah Norville talks new season
item.description: Former "Inside Edition" anchor Deborah Norville, who now hosts "The Perfect Line," joins "CBS Mornings" to discuss the show's second season.

item.title: Jane Doe in Cornell rape case facing death threats, backlash for accusations
item.description: The former Cornell student who alleges Chi Phi fraternity brothers gang raped her at a party in 2024 is receiving intense backlash for coming forward, including death threats, her lawyer told CBS News. Lilia Luciano reports.

item.title: Some Republican candidates may not want Trump's visit as he heads to Texas next to campaign
item.description: President Trump is in Texas to support Ken Paxton while other Republican candidates weigh his impact ahead of the midterms. Plus, Sen. Susan Collins of Maine defended herself on the debate stage as scrutiny of her past political decisions mounted. CBS News' Kathryn Watson and Fin Gómez report.

item.title: What younger women need to know about breast cancer
item.description: Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers in adolescents and young adults under age 39, and the rate is rising fastest in women under 50.

item.title: Christa Pike conscious and speaking after botched execution
item.description: Christa Pike is conscious and speaking after surviving two lethal injections during her execution, her attorneys said Tuesday. Skyler Henry reports.

item.title: Oct. 7, 2023, Pearl Harbor and 9/11 echo the same failures
item.description: Israel learned a lesson three years ago that America has learned, at least twice, and every time the consequences are disastrous.

item.title: Eye Opener: Tropical storm swirls near Gulf Coast
item.description: A tropical storm off the Gulf Coast could become the year's first Atlantic hurricane. Meanwhile, Christa Pike is awake after her botched execution, her lawyers say. All that and all that matters in today's Eye Opener.

item.title: Supreme Court wrestles with energy companies' bid to block major climate suit
item.description: Eight of the nine justices heard nearly two hours of oral arguments in a case involving an effort by the city and county of Boulder, Colorado, to hold energy companies accountable for the effects of global climate change.

item.title: U.S. intercepts $3 million in fuel shipments to Cuba as blockade tightens
item.description: The U.S. has intercepted 90 Cuba-bound shipments of biodiesel, widening a U.S.-imposed oil blockade aimed at choking off illegally trafficked fuel.

item.title: Shock gloves bought by ICE cause intense pain, Army study says
item.description: Participants in a military exercise felt intense pain, stopped fighting immediately and feared additional exposures, according to an Army study.

item.title: How Israeli and Palestinian kids are coping 3 years after Oct. 7 attacks
item.description: CBS News asks two teenagers, one from either side of the Israel-Gaza border, how their lives have changed since the Hamas attack three years ago.

item.title: Weeks before Election Day, the FEC can't enforce the law
item.description: The Federal Election Commission is down to just two members ahead of what's projected to be the most expensive election cycle on record.

item.title: Iran's Houthi allies deny losing ground as Mideast crisis engulfs Yemen
item.description: Iran's Houthi allies deny that they've lost ground to Yemen's Saudi-backed military, as oil prices ease despite the Middle East crisis erupting in a battle over control of another key waterway.

item.title: Christa Pike is conscious, speaking after botched execution, attorneys say
item.description: Christa Pike, a death row inmate who was subject​ to a failed execution attempt in Tennessee last week, is conscious and speaking from her hospital bed, her attorneys said Tuesday.

item.title: Eva Marie Saint, "North by Northwest" star, dies at 102
item.description: Eva Marie Saint won an Oscar for her film debut opposite Marlon Brando in "On the Waterfront." She bucked many Hollywood conventions throughout her lengthy career.
